Subject: Pricing exhibit questions: liquidated remedy and min-floor

Hi Aisha / Marissa —

Thanks again for the draft. Our legal and procurement teams flagged two items in Exhibit B that need clarification before we can move to signature:

1) Liquidated remedies: the current cap in the exhibit reads "greater of 3 months of Fees or $200,000." Counsel is asking us to either reduce the cap or include a carveout for gross negligence/intentional misconduct. Can Redwood confirm if you can either: (a) lower the numeric cap to $150k, or (b) add a carveout so the remedy cap does not apply to willful misconduct?

2) Minimum monthly floor: we have operational seasonality that makes the 50k token floor tough for Q1 — can we discuss a temporary floor step-down to 40k tokens for the first 3 months with pro-rated true-up? Procurement also asked about a short holdback (5-10%) tied to onboarding milestones.

We attached the exhibits with redline comments. Jordan (legal) copied. Can you advise what is acceptable from Redwood's side and what will require legal signoff?

Thanks,
Sam

—
Sam Torres

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit questions: liquidated remedy and min-floor

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the clear notes. Quick responses below and attaching an annotated redline from our side: pricing_exhibit_v2.pdf (see pages 2–4).

- Liquidated remedies: we can add a carveout for gross negligence and willful misconduct. We are reluctant to reduce the cap to $150k across the board given unit economics on reserved capacity, but we can propose an alternate formulation: cap = greater of (3 months Fees, $200k) but exclude amounts arising from gross negligence/willful misconduct. If Acme needs a hard lower cap for commercial reasons, we can discuss an exceptions path with sales approval.

- Minimum monthly floor: we can accept a time-limited step-down to 40k tokens for the first 90 days post-go-live with a pro-rated true-up at the end of month 3 (if actual usage < floor, the difference carries forward as a credit against future months across the next 6 months). That meets us halfway and keeps billing predictable.

- Holdback: we can accept a 7% holdback on the first two invoices, released upon completion of onboarding checklist items (SLA baseline, access to audit logs, and successful model validation). Our finance/legal will want the onboarding checklist appended to Exhibit B.

Looping Karthik to confirm the commercial tradeoffs (discount / crediting) and Laura for legal wording.

Short next steps: Marissa / Karthik to confirm whether sales will approve the $200k cap + carveout vs. lowering the cap; Laura to draft redline language for carveout and holdback milestones.

Best,
Aisha

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <s.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit questions: liquidated remedy and min-floor

Sam — quick commercial note from sales side:

- We are prepared to take the $200k cap with the carveout for willful misconduct/gross negligence. To make that palatable to revenue ops, we need the 7% onboarding holdback (as Aisha suggested) and the temporary floor step-down as proposed.

- In exchange we would request that the customer commit to a 9-month ramp schedule (i.e., the 40k floor step-down is only for months 1–3; months 4–9 revert to the contracted 50k with a 2-month gradual ramp). If Acme cannot agree to ramping language, we'd need to keep the higher floor with an additional onboarding discount of 5% in month 1.

If that trade looks acceptable, Marissa and I will update the commercial summary and drop a tracked-change redline into redline_pricing_exhibit.docx for legal to review.

Karthik
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit questions: liquidated remedy and min-floor

Hi Sam / team —

Thanks for the patience while we worked with finance and product on practical guardrails. Attached is our marked Exhibit B (redline_pricing_exhibit.docx) and the suggested legal text below — please treat as Redwood's preferred language.

Suggested redline (to insert under Section 4.2 — Remedies):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer's aggregate liability for damages arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) three (3) months' Fees payable by Customer under the Order Form; or (ii) Two Hundred Thousand US Dollars (USD 200,000); provided, however, that such limitation shall not apply to damages resulting from Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breaches of Customer Data confidentiality obligations. The parties agree that liquidated damages will not be considered punitive and are the parties' reasonable estimate of actual damages."

On holdback and onboarding: insert new Exhibit B, Section 2.3a — "Customer agrees to a seven percent (7%) holdback of the first two invoices following Go-Live. Release of holdback is conditioned on completion of onboarding milestones (SLA baseline report, audit-log access verification, and model validation sign-off). Any withheld amounts that are not released after 90 days will be credited to Customer over the subsequent six billing cycles unless otherwise agreed in writing."

On floor step-down and ramp: we will accept a temporary reduction of the monthly minimum from 50k to 40k tokens for the first ninety (90) days post-Go-Live, with a contractual ramp back to 50k by month 4 and a full return to the contracted floor by month 6. If Customer prefers no ramp, Redwood will provide a one-time 5% onboarding credit in lieu of the temporary floor step-down.

Please review the edits and let us know if Acme's counsel wants alternate wording. If Jordan is okay with the carveout language, we can issue a final clean Order Form for signature tomorrow and route a DocuSign link.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
